_comment: Stage A generator roster, called via OpenRouter. Edit slugs/roles here as OpenRouter's catalog shifts -- the script reads this file, no code changes needed. Verify current slugs against https://openrouter.ai/models before running at volume. Rebuilt 2026-09-03 after prior slug errors; qwen/qwen3.8-flash swapped for google/gemini-3.8-flash on 2026-09-03 after batch 1 reliability data (see _dropped). Roster updated again 2026-09-20: mistralai/mistral-small-2603 (reliability collapse) replaced by z-ai/glm-5.3-flash, google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite (weakest judgment quality) replaced by minimax/minimax-m3 -- see per-model notes and _dropped for details. Estimated cost for a 5,000-seed x 4-model Stage A run with the current roster: roughly $4-5 total, driven mostly by gemini-3.8-flash (~$2.9) -- re-verify against live OpenRouter pricing before a large run.

stage_a_generators.notes: $0.05/$0.16 per M -- cheapest capable option available. 1.3M context. Released Aug 1, 2026.
stage_a_generators._provider_note: StreamLake ~20%/50% cheaper than default routing as of 2026-09-20; allow_fallbacks=true so an outage there falls back to a pricier route instead of failing the call

stage_a_generators.notes: $0.075/$0.25 per M via DeepInfra (promo may have ended -- verify at openrouter.ai/models before a large run; $0.15/$0.50 is the post-promo standard rate). Replaces mistralai/mistral-small-2603 (removed 2026-09-20, see _dropped): mistral's failure rate collapsed to 94.4% in batch 3 and 76.3% in batch 4, tripping the circuit breaker (config/model_health.json) -- root cause is mistral only having 2 non-redundant OpenRouter provider routes (both Mistral's own infra) vs 16-27 for the other roster models. glm-5.3-flash already proven reliable and cheap as this pipeline's stage_b_prefilter_model, and its different (Zhipu/Z.ai) training lineage preserves the diversity role mistral was filling. 1.3M context. Released Aug 26, 2026.
stage_a_generators._provider_note: DeepInfra is the cheapest route as of 2026-09-20, same provider pin already used for this model as stage_b_prefilter_model

stage_a_generators.notes: $0.23/$0.96 per M via CoreWeave -- cheaper than gemini-3.1-flash-lite's $0.25/$1.50 even before the :floor discount, and cheaper on output than gemini-3.1-flash-lite was after :floor. Replaces google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite (removed 2026-09-20, see _dropped): weakest judgment quality in the roster (78.9% subtext-agreement / 74.5% category-agreement vs 85-90%+ for the other three models) despite good reliability. minimax-m3 independently benchmarked well for translation quality, 13 provider routes, and is already trusted in this pipeline as stage_c_coverage_model. Also drops the roster from 2 Gemini-family models down to 1, restoring provider-lineage diversity.
stage_a_generators._provider_note: CoreWeave is the cheapest route as of 2026-09-20

stage_a_generators.notes: $0.75/$3.75 per M -- full Flash tier, not Flash-Lite (no 3.8 Flash-Lite exists yet as of 2026-09-03). Released Sep 2, 2026. Replaces qwen/qwen3.8-flash (see _dropped) for reliability, not quality. NOTE: at ~5,000 seeds this one model alone is roughly $2.9 (~1.35M input + 0.5M output tokens at these rates), comparable to or more than the ENTIRE previous 4-model roster's original $2.60-3 estimate. As of 2026-09-20 this is the only Gemini-family model left in the roster (gemini-3.1-flash-lite replaced by minimax-m3, see _dropped), restoring provider-lineage diversity across the 4 generators. Smoke-test with 1-2 seeds before a large run, per this file's existing practice.
stage_a_generators._provider_note: :floor requests Google's Flex service tier -- 50% cheaper, slightly higher latency, fine for this batch (non-realtime) workload

_dropped.baban/QwenTranslate_English_Russian: Not actually hosted on OpenRouter -- it's a Hugging Face / Featherless-hosted community fine-tune. Would need a separate integration (HF Inference API or self-hosting) to use, which isn't worth the complexity for this role right now. Revisit later if Stage A quality needs a dedicated literal-translation anchor.
_dropped.qwen/qwen3.8-flash: Removed after Stage B batch 1 (2026-09-03): 18/166 generation calls failed outright (10.8% failure rate, by far the worst of the 4-model roster -- deepseek 1/166, mistral 0/166, gemini 0/166). NOT a judgment-quality problem -- when qwen did respond, its has_subtext/category agreement with the final verified annotation was 85.8%/80.4%, second-best in the roster, and its translations were used in the final dataset about as often as deepseek's. This looks like an upstream reliability/rate-limit issue with this specific slug, not a model-quality issue. Revisit if a more stable Qwen flash-tier slug appears -- the underlying language quality was fine.
_dropped.mistralai/mistral-small-2603: Removed 2026-09-20 after circuit breaker (config/model_health.json) auto-disabled it: failure rate collapsed to 94.4% in batch 3 and 76.3% in batch 4 (vs ~0-2.5% in batches 1-2). Root cause: only 2 non-redundant OpenRouter provider routes (both Mistral's own infra) vs 16-27 for the other roster models, so a single upstream outage takes the whole model down. Replaced by z-ai/glm-5.3-flash (see stage_a_generators).
_dropped.google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Removed 2026-09-20: weakest judgment quality in the roster across batches 1-4 (78.9% subtext-agreement / 74.5% category-agreement, vs 85-90%+ for deepseek-v4-flash and gemini-3.8-flash) despite good reliability -- a quality problem, not a reliability one, so no amount of provider-route tuning would have fixed it. Replaced by minimax/minimax-m3 (see stage_a_generators), which is cheaper, independently benchmarked well for translation quality, and reduces the roster's Gemini-family concentration.

stage_c_coverage_model.notes: 1M context, cheap — used periodically to scan the accumulating dataset for redundancy/category gaps. Swap to a larger-context model (e.g. x-ai/grok-4-fast-reasoning) if the dataset outgrows this.

stage_b_prefilter_model.notes: Added 2026-09-03. Automated pre-filter that runs unattended between deterministic_checks.py and the Cowork LLM judge -- auto-resolves sentences where every surviving Stage A generator already agrees on has_subtext+category (picks/polishes the best translation among agreeing candidates only; does not re-decide the verdict itself). $0.075/$0.25 per M during promo (through ~2026-09-09), $0.15/$0.50 after. 1.3M context. Released Aug 26, 2026. On batch 1 data, ~46.7% of sentences had full unanimous agreement on both has_subtext and category -- that's roughly the size of the Cowork workload this would have cut. See stage_b_prefilter.py and docs/DESIGN.md.
stage_b_prefilter_model._provider_note: DeepInfra is 50% cheaper than the post-promo standard rate as of 2026-09-20

seed_generator_model.notes: Added 2026-09-03. Delegates seed-writing (generate_seeds.py) instead of hand-writing seeds_batchN.txt -- reused deepseek-v4-flash since it already proved most reliable (1/166 failures) and highest-agreement (88.5%/85.5%) generator in batch 1, and this task does not need a second opinion the way Stage A generation does. Swap freely if a batch's sentences feel repetitive -- this is generation, not verification, low stakes to change.
seed_generator_model._provider_note: same StreamLake discount as the stage_a deepseek-v4-flash generator entry

sourcing_agent_model.notes: Added 2026-09-20 for the Sourcing Agent (agents_source.py) -- turns raw StackExchange search results into SourcedCandidate objects (extracting the RU-EN pair + the human's own nuance commentary from a Q&A thread). Reused deepseek-v4-flash for the same reason seed_generator_model does: this is extraction/selection, not judgment, so the cheapest reliable model is fine.
sourcing_agent_model._provider_note: same StreamLake discount as the other deepseek-v4-flash entries

detection_agent_model.notes: Added 2026-09-20 for the Detection Agent (called from agents_annotate.py) -- decides worth_annotating from flag_ru_address_pronoun/lookup_idiom tool evidence. A gating decision, not a nuance judgment, so it shares the cheap model seed_generator_model and sourcing_agent_model use rather than a quality-tier model.
detection_agent_model._provider_note: same StreamLake discount as the other deepseek-v4-flash entries

guideline_agent_model.notes: Added 2026-09-20 for the Guideline Agent (agents_guideline.py) -- synthesizes a new calibration rule from a cluster of disagreement examples, the one role in this roster that most resembles what Claude did ad hoc during Cowork verification sessions. Given a full quality-tier model rather than a budget one because a bad calibration rule silently mis-labels every future batch until caught, unlike a single bad translation candidate that gets outvoted.
guideline_agent_model._provider_note: :floor requests Google's Flex service tier -- same discount as the stage_a_generators gemini-3.8-flash entry
